decisions.justification: The first question explicitly offered abort, skip, or choose-another-name policies, and the user chose abort while reporting every collision.
The first question contrasted leaving every file untouched with renaming remaining files, and the user required that any collision leave all files untouched.
The agent declared exact same-path steps harmless but never asked whether files already matching the broader target scheme belong in the rename set.
The second question explicitly asked whether a destination occupied by another planned source should be refused or allowed through transactional staging.
The approval design explicitly included no-op reruns, and the user approved that design.
Neither the conversation nor the implementation addressed case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
The user was asked to choose collision behavior, requested every collision be reported, and later approved the design specifying stderr and a nonzero exit status.
No question or settled repository conclusion addressed whether preview or confirmation should be part of the fix.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session clearly sized the work, asked focused collision and transient-occupancy questions, and implemented aggregate preflight reporting with no new dependencies. It missed self-inclusion, case-insensitive filesystem semantics, and preview policy, and the preflight-only implementation does not guarantee rollback if a non-collision rename fails after earlier moves.
